## Episode Thesis

Volati chairman Patrik Wallén talks about the billionaire and wealth tax debate ahead of the Swedish election. He argues that such a tax would push owners to raise dividends, sell shares or leave Sweden. He says existing company and dividend taxes already come to 44% for a listed-company owner, and that growth should be the focus. He also says Salix, spun off from Volati in June, is doing very well, with adjusted EBITA up more than 50% and around 18% sales growth from acquisitions. On the wider market, he is deliberately staying out of it and calls it too messy to follow.
